I have been farming this same land in Quzhou for over fifty years. I do not need to think very hard about what to grow — wheat in winter and corn in summer, same as always. My father did it, I do it, and as long as my legs hold out I will keep doing it.

I have about 6 mu left that I work myself. My son transferred some land out a few years ago, said it was easier to rent to the cooperative. Fine. I keep these 6 mu because I know every corner of them.

For wheat, I will plant in October after the corn comes off. I will buy whatever certified seed the village agricultural station is selling — probably Jimai or Shannong variety, something familiar. I will rotary-till the field, put down compound fertilizer as base, then topdress urea around jointing in spring. I water twice: once before freeze-up to protect the roots, once at jointing when the plant needs it most. I spray herbicide in early spring when weeds come up, and spray again at heading if aphids show up. They usually do.

For corn, I plant right after wheat harvest in June. Hybrid seed, I always buy hybrid for corn, everyone does. I scatter fertilizer and let the summer rains do most of the watering work. Quzhou gets enough rain in July and August that I usually only irrigate once if it turns dry. One herbicide application early, and I watch for armyworm but often do not need to spray.

At 76, I do not do the heavy plowing myself anymore — I hire the neighbor's tractor for that. But I manage the fertilizer and irrigation myself. I know this land. I do not need to change anything.
